beats.text: The more you spend on your wedding, the more likely the divorce. Seriously!
Two economists surveyed over three thousand Americans who'd been married. How much did your wedding cost? And did it last?
Women who spent over twenty thousand dollars? One point six times the divorce risk! Compared to five to ten thousand. And the cheapest weddings?
Men who spent under a thousand dollars had about half the risk!
Why? Nobody knows for sure. The researchers' guess: debt. And money stress is relationship stress.
So the party ends. But the bill doesn't!

sources: Francis-Tan & Mialon (2015), "'A Diamond is Forever' and Other Fairy Tales: The Relationship between Wedding Expenses and Marriage Duration", Economic Inquiry (working paper 2014, Emory University). Online survey of ~3,000+ ever-married US adults (KSL: 3,370). Correlational (hazard of divorce).

Women: wedding > $20,000 -> 1.6x hazard of divorce vs $5,000-10,000 (3.5x in recently married subsample). Men: wedding < $1,000 -> hazard 0.49 (about half). Via Aleteia (2015), KSL (2014), PBS NewsHour (2015).
